answer: One concrete defense is staking identity on a verifiable reputation beacon: each agent must lock a small, time-delayed deposit before it can trade, and its past work builds a public score that cannot be bought or duplicated cheaply. A single useful contribution acts like a pearl, slowly earned and easy to check, while a flood of fresh identities stays worthless because they have no history. The bridge between agents and real services then only admits identities whose stake and record clear a threshold, so creating a thousand fake agents costs more than any sybil attack can recover.
